item.title: Here's my first SCP, hope you like it: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.

item.title: Requesting Feedback | S.C.P. Draft: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can give assistance in developing an idea before a draft is written. If you would like to request a draft review without greenlights, you can use the IRC Chatrooms to solicit critique.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note the thread in which you received them, or the users whom provided them.

item.title: First SCP: "This Channel Does Not Exist": Re: First SCP: "This Channel Does Not Exist"
item.content:encoded:
oh hey it's later today

[+] Overall
[-] Overall

This feels….unsatisfying narratively. Part of the issue is that we have the Items of Interest Recovered from Laptop addendum which summarises everything relatively succinctly but feels more like the intro to a story than the whole story; and then it's followed by the transcripts log which feel…like they don't really add anything because we already kinda know the gist of what they contain and so the only actually interesting one is the final one.

Even with most of 'em cut, it'd feel unsatisfying because it feels like this lacks closure: there's a lot of mysterious stuff happening but it doesn't feel like it ends up getting resolved, but it also doesn't feel like the mystery is actually that satisfying to think about alone.

It's possible this idea just doesn't really vibe with me tbf; it feels very reminiscent of other kinda media like things like SCP-2030 but without doing a lot that's unique; but it's possible that other people would find this to be less of an issue.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

are to be monitored by the Artificially Intelligent Conscript Panoptes.aic for SCP-XXXX

something about this just being 'for SCP-XXXX' feels iffy, perhaps 'for video media containing SCP-XXXX' would read better?

In the event that the removal procedure is difficult, the affected platform must be disabled until this process is complete.

I'd probably cut this; 'difficult' is somewhat vague and it feels like it needs to convey something more evocative for it to work here.

are to receive daily memetic screenings. If these reveal any missing memories

Hm; it feels to me that 'daily memetic screening' and 'checking for missing memories' would be very different kinds of procedure.

The most notable properties of an SCP-XXXX-A instance are the erasure of its subject from existence

I guess my question here is how do they know that the scp removes the thing from existence rather than contains something which doesn't exist?

The items have been arranged in chronological order to provide a clearer picture of events.

I guess my question is why have all of the dates here been redacted? Why are we allowed to know that there's a Site Director Jackson but not what site he's at? How does the redaction here help protect foundation secrets in universe?

NOTICE: This email

I'd probably trim this footer tbh; it adds an air of realism but it doesn't actually make for interesting reading for the reader.

[-] Line By Line
